objective: Allow configuration administrators to bind each release-approval scenario to a published workflow per project, with backend resolution, immutable running-version semantics, auditability and workflow lifecycle protection.
users: Configuration administrators bind five release scenarios for the current project.
Project developers submit release applications without selecting or typing workflow identifiers.
Workflow administrators maintain definitions while the platform protects referenced and historical definitions.
Auditors inspect binding changes and immutable workflow history.

requirements.statement: Configuration management must expose five fixed approval scenarios whose published-workflow bindings are isolated by tenant and project.
acceptance: project switching loads the corresponding bindings
each project and scene has at most one binding
the user selects a published workflow instead of typing a code
requirements.source: User confirmed a separate configuration-management page and project-specific bindings on 2026-08-17.
counterexample: workflow graph is edited from the binding page

requirements.statement: Projects may save partial bindings, while submission must fail atomically only when its resolved scenario is unbound or references a non-published definition.
acceptance: failed submission creates no round, instance or status transition
requirements.source: User approved fixed scenes with partial configuration and hit-time blocking.
counterexample: missing emergency binding blocks regular submissions
a failed start leaves a STARTING round

requirements.statement: The release backend must resolve the project-scene binding by workflow definition ID and freeze the actual definition version and instance on each submitted round.
acceptance: new submissions use the binding committed at submission time
existing submissions continue on their original definition version after rebinding
the frontend cannot choose a workflow in the application payload
requirements.source: User approved that binding changes affect only future applications.

requirements.statement: Binding changes must require a reason, preserve before and after values with operator and time, enforce tenant/project authorization and reject stale writes.
acceptance: create, update and unbind history is queryable
cross-project and cross-tenant access is denied
requirements.source: User approved traceable binding lifecycle behavior.
counterexample: only the final value is retained
last writer silently overwrites a concurrent update

requirements.statement: Only never-published definitions with no instances and no active business binding may be deleted; an actively bound definition may not be archived.
acceptance: a pure draft can be soft-deleted
a formerly published draft cannot be deleted
requirements.source: User confirmed workflow lifecycle and reference-protection rules.
counterexample: unpublish then delete bypasses history protection
archiving a bound definition breaks future release submissions

invariants: running instances remain bound to their original definition and version
all definitions, bindings and queries are tenant scoped
project context remains a stable interface while its current source is mocked
unrelated rokey worktree changes remain untouched
constraints: existing WorkflowBusinessGateway and release lifecycle consumer remain the integration boundary
non_goals: workflow graph editing from configuration management
manual workflow choice on a release application
automatic creation of approval graphs or assignees
changes to release scenario classification rules

selected_approach.name: project-scoped release workflow bindings
selected_approach.reason: It removes memorized codes, supports project differences and keeps workflow authoring separate with bounded module integration.

alternatives.name: hard-coded workflow codes
alternatives.rejected_because: error-prone configuration and code changes are required to remap scenarios

alternatives.name: platform-wide generic scenario center
alternatives.rejected_because: cross-module governance and scope are larger than the current release-management requirement

alternatives.name: business-purpose selection in workflow authoring
alternatives.rejected_because: it couples generic workflow authoring to release-specific scene semantics

inside: release workflow binding schema, service, API and page
workflow delete and archive reference guards

components.name: ReleaseWorkflowBindingService
components.responsibility: manage project bindings, optimistic locking, audit and submission-time resolution

components.name: ReleaseWorkflowBindingStore
components.responsibility: persist bindings and immutable binding history

components.name: ReleaseSubmissionService
components.responsibility: map the existing business scenario to a binding and start the selected published definition

components.name: WorkflowDefinitionCatalog
components.responsibility: provide tenant-scoped published candidates and definition validation

components.name: WorkflowService
components.responsibility: enforce delete and archive guards using versions, instances and business references

components.name: ReleaseApprovalWorkflowPage
components.responsibility: display five scene bindings, validity, reasoned updates and history for the current project

interfaces.name: release workflow binding API
interfaces.contract: tenant/project-scoped fixed scene list, published candidates, reasoned optimistic updates and history

interfaces.name: workflow definition catalog
interfaces.contract: read-only published-definition summaries and server-side status validation

interfaces.name: release workflow binding reference
interfaces.contract: read-only active references for archive and delete decisions without direct rel-table access

transitions: freeze definition, version and instance on round

data_flows.output: safe lifecycle transition with history preserved

error_handling.behavior: reject only the matching submission before workflow or round creation
error_handling.recovery: bind a published workflow for the current project and retry

error_handling.condition: bound definition is no longer published
error_handling.behavior: mark the binding invalid and reject submission

error_handling.recovery: reload the current binding and submit a new reasoned change

error_handling.condition: definition has history, instances or bindings
error_handling.behavior: reject delete with an explicit reason
error_handling.recovery: retain or archive after removing active bindings

error_handling.behavior: reject archive and return bounded project-scene summaries
error_handling.recovery: rebind or unbind references, then archive

security: server-authoritative project, tenant and permission checks
compatibility: existing instances and rounds need no migration
current mocked project contract remains usable
operations: no silent fallback to hard-coded codes

verification_strategy.signal: binding APIs and page show isolated fixed scenes, partial state, history and conflict behavior
verification_strategy.method: service/API tests, frontend build and authenticated browser checks across two mock projects

verification_strategy.signal: submission starts the configured definition and failures leave no partial state
verification_strategy.method: transactional integration tests and database aggregate verification

verification_strategy.signal: pure draft deletion succeeds while prior publication, instances and references block destructive lifecycle actions
verification_strategy.method: workflow service tests and API checks

verification_strategy.signal: end-to-end release submission, business-owned approval and lifecycle callback complete
verification_strategy.method: browser workflow using a published test definition and project binding

assumptions.text: the current mocked project ID remains stable until project management integration
assumptions.basis: the existing project-context contract already supplies a stable currentRef
assumptions.falsifier: the project module introduces a different canonical identifier without mapping

assumptions.text: workflow definition IDs remain stable across published versions
assumptions.basis: wf_version is keyed under wf_definition and current publishing updates current_version
assumptions.falsifier: workflow versioning is redesigned to replace definitions rather than append versions

decisions.decision: Place approval workflow configuration in configuration management, separate from workflow authoring
decisions.reason: separates business usage from graph design
projects may use different approval paths

decisions.decision: Show five fixed scenes and permit partial binding
decisions.reason: unused scenes should not block configured scenarios

decisions.decision: Binding changes affect only future submissions
decisions.reason: active workflow versions must remain immutable

decisions.decision: Only pure drafts may be deleted and active bindings block archive
decisions.reason: preserve instances, history, signatures and audit

risks.mitigation: stabilize currentRef and provide a one-time mapping when project management is integrated

risks.impact: a submission uses an unexpected definition
risks.mitigation: resolve committed binding transactionally and freeze the actual result on the round

risks.risk: workflow lifecycle creates a direct module-table dependency
risks.mitigation: use a read-only reference interface implemented by release management

risks.risk: bound workflow is unpublished outside release management
risks.mitigation: show invalid state, block clearly and log the condition rather than silently falling back

approval.evidence: User reviewed the landed design summary and explicitly requested implementation on local rokey on 2026-08-17.
